title: A randomized controlled trial in preterm infants comparing prophylactic with selective “Less Invasive Surfactant Administration”
summary: Preterm infants often have severe respiratory distress, which can be treated with a drug called surfactant. The pro.LISA trial will test if prophylactic surfactant treatment of preterm infants with moderate respiratory distress improves lung function at age 5 years.

interventions.name: Prophylactic surfactant treatment (100 mg/kg bodyweight) with less invasive surfactant administration within the first 60 minutes of life.

Selective surfactant administration if respiratory distress is worsening (e.g. FiO2 > 30% for more than 30 minutes, severe respiratory distress). Selective administration of surfactant can be done via LISA.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Preterm infants with a gestational age between 25 weeks + 0 days and 30 weeks + 6 days, 
(2) age <= 60 minutes, 
(3) spontaneous breathing on continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) with supplemental oxygen < 30%.
Exclusion criteria:
(1) Lethal malformations, (2) planned comfort care
